biography: Joachim "Jockel" Winkelhock, a name once whispered with reverence in the German touring car scene, now echoes with a touch of melancholy. Born in Waiblingen in 1960, the roar of engines was practically Jockel's lullaby, his father Manfred being a formidable racer himself. Young Joachim cut his teeth in karting, his aggressive style already evident as he elbowed his way to regional championships. The move to touring cars was inevitable, and he quickly made a name for himself, known for daring overtakes and a refusal to back down. Winkelhock's star shone brightest in the early 90s, but a series of unfortunate team changes and a slight dip in reflexes have seen him struggle to recapture that former glory. Now at 37, he clings to a seat with Team DT Racing, a shadow of his former self, desperate to prove he still has what it takes, even as younger, hungrier drivers nip at his heels.
drivingStyle: Winkelhock's driving style is a reflection of his personality: aggressive and uncompromising. He's known for late braking maneuvers that often leave rivals shaking their heads – and sometimes trading paint. While his tire management is not his strongest suit, often pushing too hard early in stints, he excels under pressure, thriving in wheel-to-wheel combat. He possesses an uncanny ability to extract every last tenth of a second from the car, often bordering on recklessness, a trait that has both won him races and landed him in the gravel trap.

rivalries.reason: A long-standing feud stemming from a controversial incident at the Norisring in '92 where Winkelhock punted Richter into the barriers while battling for the lead.
A fierce on-track rivalry fueled by mutual respect and a desire to prove themselves as the top German touring car driver.
Bellini, a young up-and-comer, publicly criticized Winkelhock's 'outdated' driving style, sparking a heated exchange and an intense battle for track position whenever they meet.

quirks: Always wears the same pair of lucky socks, hand-knitted by his grandmother, for every race.
Before each race, he listens to a specific German heavy metal song at full volume to pump himself up.
Has a habit of meticulously cleaning his racing gloves before putting them on, regardless of their actual cleanliness.
famousQuote: "Second place is just the first loser."
careerHighlight: Winning the 1991 DTM Championship after a season-long battle, securing the title with a daring final-lap overtake at Hockenheim.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead at the 24 Hours of Spa in 1995, costing his team a likely victory and severely damaging his reputation.
